newsitem.title: UK: UK's Brown says 1.5 bln stg wasted in NHS.
newsitem.headline: UK's Brown says 1.5 bln stg wasted in NHS.

text.p: British Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown said on Wednesday there was scope for saving around 1.5 billion pounds in the National Health Service which was now being wasted on excessive bureaucracy.
In an interview with BBC radio, he said the new government initially aimed to release 100 million pounds by using existing resources more effectively, but more would also be done.
"Money is being wasted on administrative changes, on bureaucracy, on the costs of the health service, which used to be eight percent on administration, now 12 and rising to 13 percent," Brown said.
The government aimed to tackle the root problem, which he said was a mis-direction of resources in the health service under the previous Conservative government.
"We're actually talking about an extra one and a half billion pounds now spent on paper, administration, bureaucracy, BMWs for administrators, when it should go to patient care," he said.
